progress: Mixed, a presidential directive to digitalise four named services against a strategy still pre-adoption and a service bus that has never operated
summary: The President [directed all agencies to digitalise passports, identity cards, licences and procurement](2026-02-16 Malawi President orders digital revolution), while a [draft transformation strategy](2026-02-20 Malawi validates AI strategy, digital transformation policy - CAJ News Africa) is still in validation under the [2023-28 digitalisation policy](2026-05-20-local-authorities-ict-policy-dowa-malawi24).
developments:
The directive was given in the State of the Nation Address against a target of 80 per cent internet usage by 2026, with no baseline given against which it could be assessed ([directive](2026-02-16 Malawi President orders digital revolution)); of the four named services only public procurement is evidenced as delivered inside the window ([directive](2026-02-16 Malawi President orders digital revolution)).

A draft national digital transformation strategy went to a validation workshop in February 2026 and remains pre-adoption ([validation](2026-02-20 Malawi validates AI strategy, digital transformation policy - CAJ News Africa), [consultations](2025-09-25-national-ai-strategy-consultation-itweb)).

The 2023-28 policy remains the reference framework, with the e-government department under pressure to onboard all agencies onto the service bus intended to let ministries exchange data ([framework](2026-05-20-local-authorities-ict-policy-dowa-malawi24), [implementation](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times), [enforcement](2026-01-27-ict-sector-eyes-policy-enforcement-times)).

summary: A [draft National AI Strategy](2026-02-20 Malawi validates AI strategy, digital transformation policy - CAJ News Africa) has been through validation and a citizen-feedback portal, guided by a [readiness assessment](2026-07-24-malawi-strengthen-ai-ecosystem) validated in July 2026.
developments:
Regional consultative workshops began in September 2025 and a two-day validation workshop was held in Lilongwe in February 2026; the strategy is pre-adoption with no adoption date on record ([workshops](2025-09-25-national-ai-strategy-consultation-itweb), [validation](2026-02-20 Malawi validates AI strategy, digital transformation policy - CAJ News Africa), [assessment](2026-07-24-malawi-strengthen-ai-ecosystem)).

The readiness assessment was validated in July 2026 to guide it, finding gaps in policy, infrastructure, institutional capacity and education readiness, with 27.7 per cent of the population online against household computer ownership of 4.2 per cent ([readiness](2026-07-24-malawi-strengthen-ai-ecosystem)). It was run by the education ministry rather than the ICT ministry that owns the strategy ([regional framework](2026-06-26-itweb-sadc-regional-ai-strategy-regulatory-framework)).

summary: Spectrum licence fees were [cut by 20 per cent](2025-06-25-macra-spectrum-fees-cut-20pc-ecofin) and the regulator is building a [harmonised national broadband map](2026-08-25-itu-sub-saharan-broadband-push) under a regional project.
developments:
The reduction across all bands followed review of the regulator's 2016 incentive pricing model; no fee schedule, gazette notice or statutory instrument is held, so the base amounts and the effective date are unknown ([reduction](2025-06-25-macra-spectrum-fees-cut-20pc-ecofin), [account](2025-06-26-macra-spectrum-fees-cut-20pc-techafricanews)). The minister told Parliament in July 2026 that the cut was 50 per cent ([reduction](2025-06-25-macra-spectrum-fees-cut-20pc-ecofin)); five contemporaneous accounts say 20 and no source records a second reduction ([parliament](2026-07-18-namalomba-parliament-new-operators-nyasatimes)).

The regulator hosted a five-day training at Lilongwe in August 2026 for broadband-mapping practitioners from four countries, under a 2025-2028 project to establish harmonised national broadband mapping in eleven sub-Saharan regulators ([mapping](2026-08-25-itu-sub-saharan-broadband-push)).

summary: The [Data Protection Act 2024](2024-02-02-malawi-data-protection-act-2024) exempted most controllers for twenty-four months from commencement, and that exemption elapsed in early June 2026.
developments:
The Act commenced in June 2024 with the regulator designated data protection authority, and exempted controllers and processors not of significant importance from compliance for twenty-four months, so most of the economy sat outside its obligations ([Act](2024-02-02-malawi-data-protection-act-2024)).

The general exemption elapsed in early June 2026 so that all controllers and processors are now within scope, while the subsidiary instruments to operate registration and enforcement were still in draft ([compliance](2026-07-16-macra-data-protection-registration-compliance-malawi24), [terms of reference](2025-10-01-dmap-tor-operationalization-data-protection-authority)). The commencement day cannot be settled from this base: the circulating expiry date implies a 2 June 2024 commencement and the commencement notice is not held.

summary: An [AI Bill](2026-08-20-timesmw-malawi-government-eyes-ai-laws) is targeted to reach parliament before December 2026, and the [copyright body will not register wholly AI-generated works](2026-07-23-malawi24-cosoma-ai-music-rules).
developments:
The bill is announced as the statutory backing for the strategy, to establish a framework promoting innovation while safeguarding citizen privacy and ensuring operational accountability; the minister put the target at before December 2026, no draft text is stated, and the strategy it would ground is itself pre-adoption ([bill](2026-08-20-timesmw-malawi-government-eyes-ai-laws), [drafting](2026-08-10-malawi-drafts-ai-bill), [scope](2026-08-06-malawi-drafts-ai-bill-to-govern-public-sector-tech)).

The statutory copyright body will not register works created entirely by artificial intelligence or distribute royalties on them; the rule is known only as reported, with no test stated for how much assistance is admissible, and the body's own statement is not held ([rule](2026-07-23-malawi24-cosoma-ai-music-rules)).

summary: A [financial crimes amendment](2026-08-07-malawi-mps-digital-finance-reform-bills) removing all references to cheques passed Parliament in August 2026, one of four bills effecting the cheque phase-out.
developments:
The bill was passed alongside amendments to the payment systems and deposit insurance statutes, following a bills of exchange amendment that effects the phase-out ([bills](2026-08-07-malawi-mps-digital-finance-reform-bills)).

Assent, gazette date and commencement are not published, and the safeguarding regulations the finance minister promised are not drafted. A member warned that rural users risk being left behind by the switch away from cheques ([warning](2026-08-06-mcp-mp-warns-rural-malawi-risks-being-left-behind-in-switch-away-from-cheques)), and the base holds no primary for the discontinuation itself and no date for it.

summary: A proposed [government data sharing regulation](2026-06-11-government-data-sharing-regulation-boma-lathu-itweb) would route all data requests through the national data centre and require binding sharing agreements, and it is not made.
developments:
Ministries and agencies had been sharing citizen data by email, USB drive and paper, and the platform operated without binding rules ([regulation](2026-06-11-government-data-sharing-regulation-boma-lathu-itweb)).

The proposal would require encryption in transit and at rest, set a common digital standard for system-to-system exchange, and require binding data sharing agreements with usage limits and audit trails. No draft text is held, and the minister described a binding regulation as the missing piece in an account given during a vendor meeting abroad.

summary: The [National Registration Act is under review](2026-07-13 Malawi outlines plans to transition to digital IDs - CAJ News Africa) and [registration service fees were raised](2026-08-17-malawi-nrb-registration-fees-e-kyc) by regulations gazetted in July 2026.
developments:
A consultative meeting under the acceleration project reviewed the registration Act and the marriage and family relations statute, the bureau stating the aim is a modern and secure civil registration and identification system; no bill, draft or timetable is on record ([review](2026-07-13 Malawi outlines plans to transition to digital IDs - CAJ News Africa)).

Amendment regulations gazetted on 31 July 2026 raised fees for identity card replacement, electronic know-your-customer verification, civil registration and marriage services; the individual levels and their previous values are not carried in the record held, so the size of the increase is not established, and the electronic verification charge is a charge on third parties for using the identity system ([fees](2026-08-17-malawi-nrb-registration-fees-e-kyc)).

summary: The [authority now operates as a unit inside the regulator](2026-07-16-macra-data-protection-registration-compliance-malawi24) with a named head, [draft regulations and a registration fee schedule](2026-07-14-macra-data-protection-registration-fees-consultation-itweb) out for consultation, and [independence stated as intended](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews).
developments:
The unit has a named head of data protection and a stated implementation framework, with no organogram, enforcement record or registration data published ([unit](2026-07-16-macra-data-protection-registration-compliance-malawi24)).

Draft regulations, guidelines and a turnover-based registration fee schedule ranging from MWK 50,000 for small and medium enterprises to MWK 7 million for the largest controllers of significant importance were published and consulted on before finalisation ([fees](2026-07-14-macra-data-protection-registration-fees-consultation-itweb)); no commencement date is on record ([fees](2026-07-14-macra-data-protection-registration-fees-consultation-itweb), [consultation](2026-07-16-macra-data-protection-registration-compliance-malawi24)).

The regulator states it intends to establish both the authority and the response team as independent institutions with donor technical assistance, with no legislative vehicle, timetable or funding model on record ([separation](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews)); a consultancy to design the authority's structure was tendered in October 2025 with no award on file ([consultancy](2025-10-01-dmap-tor-operationalization-data-protection-authority)).

summary: A delegation went to [Accra to structure digital-government cooperation](2026-08-25-malawi-ghana-digital-government-support-biometricupdate), the minister [urged regional artificial-intelligence investment priorities](2026-08-20-malawi-urges-comesa-to-target-ai-investments), and the [regulator opened talks with a development agency](2026-07-10-macra-undp-ai-digital-id-collaboration-itweb).
developments:
The Accra visit was to structure cooperation under which Ghana is to make more than a dozen technology companies available to help build systems and infrastructure, with Ghana's identity card cited as the reference implementation and Malawi bringing a high-coverage identity system, a data centre and a data exchange; no memorandum, budget or timetable is named ([visit](2026-08-25-malawi-ghana-digital-government-support-biometricupdate)).

At a regional workshop in Lilongwe the minister named agriculture, healthcare, climate resilience, education, financial services and regional trade as bloc investment priorities, framing connectivity, data quality, skills and cybersecurity policy as the precondition; no bloc decision, instrument or envelope follows it ([priorities](2026-08-20-malawi-urges-comesa-to-target-ai-investments)).

Regulator talks with a development agency named identity integration with SIM verification, responsible artificial intelligence, data protection and secondary-school skills as priorities, with no memorandum, funding figure or timetable ([talks](2026-07-10-macra-undp-ai-digital-id-collaboration-itweb)).

summary: A [regional declaration on collaborative regulation](2026-05-04-research-ict-africa-crasa-lilongwe-declaration-collaborative-regulation) was adopted at a Lilongwe summit in April 2026, and a [regional AI framework](2026-06-26-itweb-sadc-regional-ai-strategy-regulatory-framework) is claimed to be under development.
developments:
The declaration anchors to an international regulatory maturity framework, sets six shared principles and seven areas of collaborative action, and treats artificial intelligence, satellite, digital platforms and next-generation networks as one emerging-technology frontier; the regional association has not published the text, so the whole account is named-analyst commentary and the seven action areas are nowhere enumerated ([declaration](2026-05-04-research-ict-africa-crasa-lilongwe-declaration-collaborative-regulation)).

A regional artificial-intelligence strategy and regulatory framework is reported under development with no draft, adoption date or document title beyond the name; the claim is the Malawian ministry's rather than the regional secretariat's, so any statement that the region has such a framework is unestablished ([framework](2026-06-26-itweb-sadc-regional-ai-strategy-regulatory-framework)).

progress: Mixed, a device-assembly allocation and a partly funded registration campaign against no school-connectivity line at all
summary: The 2026/27 budget has [no dedicated line for school internet connectivity](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24), [MWK 1.1bn for device assembly](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24) at one university, and [MWK 12.4bn of the birth-registration campaign unfunded](2026-01-16-birth-registration-campaign-4.6m-children-malawi24).
developments:
The 2026/27 budget policy statement carries no dedicated line for school internet connectivity or digital infrastructure in primary and secondary schools; education received MWK 1.28tn, 11.7 per cent of the budget, and transport and ICT received MWK 664.4bn directed at roads, rail and aviation ([budget](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24)).

MWK 1.1bn was set aside for assembling laptops and tablets at the science and technology university, the nearest digital allocation to schools in that budget and directed at higher education ([allocation](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24)).

The birth registration campaign requires MWK 17.8bn to register about 4.6 million children across seven phases; MWK 5.4bn was allocated for phases one and two, leaving MWK 12.4bn unfunded, and the figures are the minister's rather than an appropriation document ([campaign](2026-01-16-birth-registration-campaign-4.6m-children-malawi24), [partnership](2026-02-04 10 years of a fruitful partnership with the Government of Malawi on civil registration)).

summary: The [acceleration project](2024-05-05-dmap-world-bank-appraisal-pid) runs at US$90m on towers, data-centre upgrade and e-services, beside an [inclusive transformation programme](2024-01-01-ec-mwi-001-inclusive-digital-transformation-for-malawi-idt4m) and an [institutional support grant](2021-01-01-afdb-mwi-001-malawi---support-for-digitalization-financial).
developments:
The acceleration project was approved in June 2024 at US$90.00m, a US$70.00m grant plus US$20.00m commercial financing, targeting 2,000 schools, 500 further government offices, identity enrolment and an affordable-devices programme ([appraisal](2024-05-05-dmap-world-bank-appraisal-pid)); procurement for more than 90 towers is being advanced, the national data centre is being upgraded to an artificial-intelligence-ready state, and 25 e-services are being onboarded ([appraisal](2024-05-05-dmap-world-bank-appraisal-pid), [progress](2026-03-26-dmap-90-telecom-towers-rural-connectivity-techafricanews)).

An inclusive digital transformation programme runs 2024-2028 on EUR 2,000,000 and US$5,608,640, covering inclusive digital identity, open-source public systems and youth literacy ([programme](2024-01-01-ec-mwi-001-inclusive-digital-transformation-for-malawi-idt4m), [agency record](2024-01-01-undp-mwi-idt4m-2024-inclusive-digital-transformation-for-malawi-idt4m)); a bilateral grant was disbursed to the same agency for the 2025 activity year ([grant](2025-01-01-iati-xm-dac-21-1-2025000132b1mlwoc1pol-undp-inclusive-digital-transformation-malawi)).

An institutional support grant of XDR 10,000,000 had US$5,591,335 disbursed at retrieval, with no event in the window on file ([support](2021-01-01-afdb-mwi-001-malawi---support-for-digitalization-financial)).

summary: A proposed [US$180m four-year vendor investment plan](2026-06-09-huawei-180m-ict-investment-plan-malawi24) is built round a one-stop government platform and a [network linking all 28 districts](2026-06-09-huawei-180m-ict-investment-plan-malawi24), with no agreement made public.
developments:
The roadmap was presented to the vendor in China in June 2026: a one-stop digital government platform covering passport applications, business registration and tax payments, and a high-speed network linking all twenty-eight districts with ring protection against cable failures ([plan](2026-06-09-huawei-180m-ict-investment-plan-malawi24), [account](2026-06-11-government-data-sharing-regulation-boma-lathu-itweb)).

Funding structure, implementation timeline and any agreements reached have not been made public, and the base holds no signed instrument, only the ministry's account of a meeting ([status](2026-06-09-huawei-180m-ict-investment-plan-malawi24)).

summary: The second mobile operator states [US$31m invested](2026-08-17-malawi-tnm-network-investment) in network capacity and coverage, and a bank committed [MWK 75.5m and a three-year memorandum](2025-11-19-nbm-ictam-innovation-jam-ai-malawi24) to an innovation event.
developments:
The operator's figure carries no period, site count or coverage outcome, and the commitment date is not stated ([investment](2026-08-17-malawi-tnm-network-investment)).

A three-year memorandum commits a bank to mentorship, incubation and technical support for innovators emerging from an annual innovation event, with MWK 75,500,000 given to the 2025 edition ([memorandum](2025-11-19-nbm-ictam-innovation-jam-ai-malawi24)); the base records no outcome for any cohort, no count of ideas incubated, funded or surviving ([memorandum](2025-11-19-nbm-ictam-innovation-jam-ai-malawi24)).

progress: Mixed, 5G launched and expanding against fourth-generation coverage of 87 per cent that only 12.5 per cent of people use
summary: An [industry report puts 4G coverage at 87 per cent against mobile-internet penetration of 12.5](2026-08-13-digital-africa-summit-heads-to-malawi-as-the-country-enters-its-next-digital-cha), while [5G launched in 2025](2025-07-26-tnm-5g-launch-malawi-2063-malawi24) and reached [111 sites](2026-05-22-airtel-satellite-connectivity-agm-techafricanews) on the other network.
developments:
The industry association's report gives fourth-generation coverage at 87 per cent of the population against mobile-internet penetration of 12.5 per cent, scores the country 36 of 100 on its digital nations index and 55 of 100 on policy and regulation, and describes mobile-money adoption as near universal ([report](2026-08-13-digital-africa-summit-heads-to-malawi-as-the-country-enters-its-next-digital-cha)); it is the association's own index and the base holds no official national subscriber and coverage series ([report](2026-08-13-digital-africa-summit-heads-to-malawi-as-the-country-enters-its-next-digital-cha)).

The first 5G network launched at Lilongwe in July 2025 with four further cities named as extension targets, and no later site count is held for it ([launch](2025-07-26-tnm-5g-launch-malawi-2063-malawi24)).

The other operator reported 111 sites across ten districts, after 58 new sites on MWK 50.8bn of network capital expenditure in the 2025 financial year ([sites](2026-05-22-airtel-satellite-connectivity-agm-techafricanews)), and a fixed-wireless operator extended 4G coverage to nineteen neighbourhoods of the capital ([fixed wireless](2026-08-11-itweb-lilongwe-expanded-4g-access)).

progress: No change, four fifths of the population offline with no state measurement to set against the presidential target
summary: [80 per cent of Malawians are offline](2026-08-20-gsma-malawi-digital-transformation-report) despite 87 per cent fourth-generation coverage, and no state measurement is held against the target of 80 per cent usage by 2026.
developments:
The appraisal document put internet use at around 24 per 100 inhabitants on a 2022 baseline against a regional average of 28 ([appraisal](2024-05-05-dmap-world-bank-appraisal-pid)), and a separate account put access at about 20 per cent of citizens ([access](2024-05-14 Malawi on path to inclusion with digital ID project supported by EU, UNDP)).

The first usable current figure comes from the operators' trade association, which puts 80 per cent of the population offline against 87 per cent coverage, so the gap is usage rather than coverage, and estimates MWK 1.1 trillion of economic value and 490,000 jobs by 2030 from closing it ([report](2026-08-20-gsma-malawi-digital-transformation-report)). That is a modelled figure from an interested party whose policy asks include cutting the taxes its members pay.

The presidential target of 80 per cent usage by 2026 is a target and not a measurement, with no baseline given ([target](2026-02-16 Malawi President orders digital revolution)).

summary: The minister called for [scrapping the 10 per cent internet surtax and reviewing the 17.5 per cent smartphone value-added tax](2026-08-21-malawi-targets-smartphone-tax-relief), targeting 30 per cent mobile internet usage by 2030.
developments:
The call was made at a Lilongwe summit in August 2026, setting a target of raising mobile internet usage from 12.5 per cent to at least 30 per cent by 2030 ([call](2026-08-21-malawi-targets-smartphone-tax-relief)).

No budget measure, bill or instrument is on record: the treasury has published nothing and no timetable is given. It is a ministerial statement at a summit, and it is the only affordability position the base holds for the country.

summary: Two [concessional loans](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-693-million) financed the fibre backbone with no route length or operating status published, and [procurement for more than 90 towers](2026-03-26-dmap-90-telecom-towers-rural-connectivity-techafricanews) is advancing against a requirement above 1,000.
developments:
Phase one was financed by a concessional loan of CNY 155,432,330 committed in 2016 ([phase one](2016-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-001-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-1554-million)) and phase two by CNY 693,000,000 at 1 per cent over twenty years, on-lent to the electricity utility with CNY 299,286,770 drawn as at June 2023 ([phase two](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-693-million)). The base holds the two loan records and no statement of route kilometres, completion, operator or current operating status.

Tower procurement for more than 90 towers is being advanced against a project commitment of around 100, while a study cited at the same meeting puts the requirement for nationwide coverage above 1,000 towers ([towers](2026-03-26-dmap-90-telecom-towers-rural-connectivity-techafricanews), [project](2024-05-05-dmap-world-bank-appraisal-pid)).

A separate commercial loan covering 136 tower installations and last-mile fibre has no progress report, disbursement figure or completion statement on file ([loan](2019-01-01-ccb-mwi-001-china-construction-bank-provides-569-million)).

summary: Wholesale bandwidth [fell from about US$460 per Mbit/s a month in 2017 to below US$10 at 2024](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities), and no price for 2025 or 2026 is held.
developments:
The fall was reported at the close of the foundations project, on the lender's own figures ([close](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities), [account](2025-06-24 Malawi boosts digital economy with connectivity, plans 2M digital ID enrollments)).

No wholesale price for 2025 or 2026 is held, so whether the gain has held is not established, and a 2024 appraisal instead gives about US$35 per Mbit/s ([appraisal](2025-06-24 Malawi boosts digital economy with connectivity, plans 2M digital ID enrollments)), which the base does not reconcile.

summary: [Thirty rural schools were connected by satellite](2026-06-18-malawi-starlink-rural-schools), and an operator [signalled interest in satellite backhaul](2026-05-22-airtel-satellite-connectivity-agm-techafricanews) at its annual meeting.
developments:
Thirty rural schools were reported connected, serving 100,000 students and 1,500 teachers on a company announcement ([schools](2026-06-18-malawi-starlink-rural-schools)); responsibility for the recurring subscription cost is not stated, and the student figure averages over 3,000 per school without reconciliation ([schools](2026-06-18-malawi-starlink-rural-schools), [preparation](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities)).

An operator signalled interest in satellite connectivity to complement terrestrial networks in hard-to-reach areas and improve resilience, with no partner, licence, capital allocation or timetable stated ([interest](2026-05-22-airtel-satellite-connectivity-agm-techafricanews)).

The base holds no satellite licence date, licence terms or subscriber figure for the country.

summary: The [national data centre](2026-07-07 Malawi integrates immigration e-services) is the local-hosting base for the data exchange and is being upgraded, and the [revenue authority has a secondary facility](2026-08-14-malawi-mra-backup-data-centre-world-bank) in service.
developments:
The national facility was built in Lilongwe under the foundations project on a hyper-converged design with Blantyre as secondary and backup ([construction](2024-03-01 Government Data Center making progress), [delivery](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities)). It now hosts the data exchange used by the revenue authority and the registration bureau, with 25 e-services being onboarded, and is being upgraded to an artificial-intelligence-ready state ([upgrade](2026-06-11-government-data-sharing-regulation-boma-lathu-itweb), [integration](2026-07-07 Malawi integrates immigration e-services)). No commissioning date, floor area, rack count, delivered load or tier certification is held.

The revenue authority's secondary data centre is in service with power upgrades, reported as improving continuity and customs-duty accuracy at border posts and the airport, financed under a six-year regional trade project; no capacity, location or availability figure is given ([secondary](2026-08-14-malawi-mra-backup-data-centre-world-bank)).

progress: Mixed, a first commercial facility in operation while only 3 per cent of web content is served from inside the country
summary: A [commercial data centre](2026-05-01-sparc-systems-data-centre-launch-malawi24) opened in Lilongwe in 2026 and an [operator third facility](2026-03-06-tnm-third-data-centre-volte-itweb) passed its stated build window, against [3 per cent of content served locally](2026-06-09 Beyond the Homepage Measuring What It Really Takes to Keep Web Traffic Local).
developments:
The commercial facility is in operation offering local hosting, positioned against the foreign-currency cost and data-ownership exposure of offshore hosting; capacity, tier and pricing are not stated and the account is company-reported ([facility](2026-05-01-sparc-systems-data-centre-launch-malawi24)).

An operator announced a third data centre for construction within three months in March 2026; that period ended in June and the base holds no record of a start, a site or a completion ([third centre](2026-03-06-tnm-third-data-centre-volte-itweb)).

A byte-weighted measurement puts 3 per cent of web content served locally and 62 per cent regionally, primarily from South Africa, the lowest local share among the economies in the study ([locality](2026-06-09 Beyond the Homepage Measuring What It Really Takes to Keep Web Traffic Local)); it is a single measurement on a methodology the publisher describes as under development ([locality](2026-06-09 Beyond the Homepage Measuring What It Really Takes to Keep Web Traffic Local)).

progress: No change, a first electricity price figure with nothing earlier behind it
summary: An [8 per cent rise in electricity tariffs](2026-07-18-namalomba-parliament-new-operators-nyasatimes) was cited by both mobile operators in support of an average 55 per cent tariff increase application.
developments:
The figure was given by the minister in Parliament alongside a roughly 144 per cent rise in fuel prices, against which the regulator approved 22.2 per cent for one operator and 26 per cent for the other ([figures](2026-07-18-namalomba-parliament-new-operators-nyasatimes)).

All the figures are the minister's, no base period is given for either percentage, and no primary from the electricity regulator or utility is held. It is the only electricity price evidence in the country's digital record.

summary: An operator states it covers [85 per cent of the population and is working to reach the remaining 15 through solar-powered infrastructure](2025-11-10-tnm-30-years-ai-labs-times).
developments:
The statement was made at the operator's thirtieth-anniversary event, with no site count, capital allocation, target date or partner stated, and foreign-exchange shortages named as the operator's biggest challenge ([statement](2025-11-10-tnm-30-years-ai-labs-times)).

It is the only network-energy item the base holds for the country, and it is an intention rather than a programme.

summary: The [foundations project](2017-06-05-wb-mwi-001-digital-malawi-program-phase-i-malawi) connected some 640 government sites and delivered the data centre and exchange before closing in 2024, and the [research network](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities) has had no position published since.
developments:
The project closed in October 2024 with US$72.4m committed and US$72.6m disbursed, having delivered the national data centre, the data exchange and the first phase of e-procurement, connected some 640 government sites against a target of 400, and over 100 free public Wi-Fi spots ([project](2017-06-05-wb-mwi-001-digital-malawi-program-phase-i-malawi)); the base holds no post-closure evaluation and no independent verification of results, which are the lender's own ([project](2017-06-05-wb-mwi-001-digital-malawi-program-phase-i-malawi)).

The research and education network gave over 83,000 students across 81 institutions cheaper connectivity over 2017 to 2024, and no institutional membership, bandwidth, governance or funding position has been published since project close ([network](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities), [report](2025-06-24 Malawi boosts digital economy with connectivity, plans 2M digital ID enrollments)).

summary: An [automated human resource and payroll platform](2026-08-06-malawi-drafts-ai-bill-to-govern-public-sector-tech) is in pilot before rollout across ministries, Parliament, the Judiciary and local councils.
developments:
No supplier, cost, pilot scale or rollout date is stated, and nothing is stated on how personnel and payroll data is handled under the data protection statute ([platform](2026-08-06-malawi-drafts-ai-bill-to-govern-public-sector-tech)).

It is the first government-wide administrative system in the base for the country, and it is reported from the department's own account at a meeting of heads of information technology rather than from a procurement or a project document.

progress: Mixed, a response team and donor assistance in place against a state company defrauded of K700m and no strategy or incident statistics at all
summary: The [response team sits inside the regulator](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews) with no incident statistics held, [donor assistance was announced](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews), and a [state oil company was defrauded of K700m](2026-08-24-malawi24-nocma-k700m-cyber-heist).
developments:
The response team operates within the regulator with no establishing instrument, timetable, budget, staffing or incident statistics held; the only source is a two-paragraph trade report ([team](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews)).

Technical assistance covering critical-infrastructure security, legal and regulatory frameworks, data-protection systems and regional capability was outlined at a Blantyre meeting, with no amount, financing instrument, duration or workplan stated ([assistance](2026-03-26-world-bank-cybersecurity-data-protection-support-techafricanews)).

The state oil company was defrauded of K700m after attackers hijacked email from a foreign contractor and supplied false banking details, the company instructing its bank in April 2026 to wire US$403,605 to a fraudulent account ([fraud](2026-08-24-malawi24-nocma-k700m-cyber-heist)); it attributed the control weakness to a procurement model introduced before operational and cybersecurity procedures were in place ([fraud](2026-08-24-malawi24-nocma-k700m-cyber-heist)). The country is separately the only one of five studied to have rejected a foreign safe-city surveillance package ([rejection](2023-09-27-ids-mapping-supply-surveillance-technologies-africa-1bn)).

progress: Mixed, the data exchange in use by two agencies with a third integrating while the service bus has never operated
summary: The [national data exchange](2026-07-07 Malawi integrates immigration e-services) is in use by two agencies with 25 e-services being onboarded, while the [enterprise service bus](2026-01-27-ict-sector-eyes-policy-enforcement-times) is still not operating.
developments:
The exchange was delivered under the foundations project and is in use by the revenue authority and the registration bureau, hosted on locally managed servers, with the immigration department integrating while retaining data ownership; being onboarded is not live, and the base holds no count of services actually in service ([exchange](2026-07-07 Malawi integrates immigration e-services), [integration](2026-06-11-government-data-sharing-regulation-boma-lathu-itweb)).

Nothing on file establishes the service bus operating; its failure to come into service left ministries siloed and denied online passport registration and driver's licence payments, and industry voices were still pressing for all agencies to be onboarded in January 2026 ([bus](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times), [pressure](2026-01-27-ict-sector-eyes-policy-enforcement-times)).

Farmers across fourteen districts still use non-interoperable platforms, logging into each separately, and the harmonising framework for agricultural data remains a proposal ([agriculture](2025-12-05-farmer-data-interoperability-nagdi-dpi-times)).

summary: [Over 13.5m adults hold a national digital identity](2026-07-13 Malawi reaches 13.5M digital IDs as universal coverage comes into view), about [99 per cent of those aged 16 and over](2026-07-13 Malawi reaches 13.5M digital IDs as universal coverage comes into view), up from 12.5m a year earlier.
developments:
The registration system has been in operation since the National Registration Act came into force in 2015, with 12.5m enrolled and links to over 33 public and private institutions recorded in May 2025 ([system](2025-05-28 Malawi nears full scale digital ID rollout to streamline access to services)).

The count reached over 12.8m adult identities in January 2026 ([intermediate](2026-01-16-birth-registration-campaign-4.6m-children-malawi24)) and over 13.5m by July, about 99 per cent of the eligible population, with over 150,000 enrolled between April and June 2026 of whom 53 per cent were women ([coverage](2026-07-13 Malawi reaches 13.5M digital IDs as universal coverage comes into view), [baseline](2025-05-21 NRB to roll out digital ID by 2026)).

It is the highest identity coverage in this pass, and the registry's own figure is preferred over external accounts describing coverage as already complete.

summary: A [mobile identity wallet](2026-06-11-nrb-nzika-wallet-digital-id-september-itweb) was announced for September 2026 and a separate [blockchain identity wallet](2026-08-05-undp-malawi-blockchain-digital-id-wallet-recognition) is in pilot, and the base cannot establish whether they are the same product.
developments:
The mobile wallet was named and announced for a September 2026 launch, complementing rather than replacing the plastic card, requiring prior registration and needing no periodic renewal; it was not live in August 2026, and rights advocates have flagged equal-access, rural-exclusion, cybersecurity and literacy caveats ([wallet](2026-06-11-nrb-nzika-wallet-digital-id-september-itweb), [launch](2026-07-06-digital-id-cards-september-launch-times), [target](2025-05-21 NRB to roll out digital ID by 2026)).

A blockchain-enabled wallet built by a development agency with an international computing centre is in pilot before nationwide rollout, with credentials to extend to birth certificates, driving licences and marriage certificates; no pilot scale, rollout date or cost is stated, and nothing is stated on how the arrangement sits under the data protection statute ([blockchain](2026-08-05-undp-malawi-blockchain-digital-id-wallet-recognition), [plan](2025-05-28 Malawi nears full scale digital ID rollout to streamline access to services)).

Neither announcement names the other.

summary: [Mandatory biometric SIM registration](2025-05-21 Malawi to Launch Mandatory Biometric SIM Registration in July 2025) authenticates against the identity system, and no completion figure, compliance rate or closure date is held.
developments:
The programme began in July 2025 with a registration window to September, run by the regulator with the registration bureau, allowing fewer than ten cards per person per operator and carrying non-compliance fines up to MWK 50,000 daily for individuals and MWK 150,000 for corporates ([programme](2025-05-21 Malawi to Launch Mandatory Biometric SIM Registration in July 2025)).

The regulator and a development agency named integration of the identity system with SIM verification as a priority area still being explored in July 2026 ([exploration](2026-07-10-macra-undp-ai-digital-id-collaboration-itweb)), which sits awkwardly with a 2025 programme already authenticating against that system.

summary: A [national birth registration campaign](2026-01-16-birth-registration-campaign-4.6m-children-malawi24) runs seven phases across 25 districts targeting about 4.6m unregistered children, using primary schools as registration centres.
developments:
The campaign's first phase was witnessed at Dedza; the bureau had registered about 3.8m children since 2015 as at January 2026 ([campaign](2026-01-16-birth-registration-campaign-4.6m-children-malawi24), [partnership](2026-02-04 10 years of a fruitful partnership with the Government of Malawi on civil registration)).

MWK 17.8bn is required in total, MWK 5.4bn was allocated for phases one and two, and MWK 12.4bn is outstanding. No mid-campaign registration total is on record.

summary: [6,500 electoral management devices](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times) were deployed for voter verification at the September 2025 elections, with offline glitches reported at rural polling stations.
developments:
The voter register is held electronically and the devices were deployed for verification at the elections of 16 September 2025 ([deployment](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)).

Two million voters had been registered using offline digital identities in 2024. The commission had refused an observer coalition electronic access to the roll in June 2025 ([refusal](2025-06-08 MEC Rejects Observer Coalition's Electronic Voter Register Access Request)), so the register is digital for the commission's own use and not for scrutiny of it.

summary: The [National Addressing System Project](2024-02-12 National Addressing Project - MACRA Website) has had nothing published about it since February 2024, and the absence of any update is itself the finding.
developments:
The regulator-coordinated programme would give every property a physical address, spanning a national postcode system, addressing standards, an address database, physical infrastructure and geographic information systems ([project](2024-02-12 National Addressing Project - MACRA Website)).

No completion date and no delivery figure were given then, and nothing dated after February 2024 is held, so the position is carried forward rather than re-established.

summary: The [Land Information Management System](2026-08-04-malawi-reviews-digital-land-workflows) has been live since February 2024, and which transactions remain on paper is still unpublished.
developments:
The web-based system links lands, surveys and physical planning, allowing parcel viewing, document submission, notifications and payment of ground rent and application fees; the scope of remaining manual transactions is not published ([system](2026-08-04-malawi-reviews-digital-land-workflows)).

The ministry convened a workflow review in August 2026 to design digital procedures for transactions still on paper; which transactions remain manual, when revised workflows will be implemented and current processing times all remain unpublished.

summary: About [8,000 landlords were registered for rental income tax](2026-07-20-malawi24-mra-electronic-invoicing-system-momentum) through property-registration exercises across low- and high-density areas.
developments:
The drive was announced in February 2026, starting in the three main cities with data collectors recruited ([announcement](2026-02-11-malawi24-mra-clarifies-eis-rental-income-tax)), and about 8,000 landlords had registered by July ([progress](2026-07-20-malawi24-mra-electronic-invoicing-system-momentum)).

It is a registry drive riding on a revenue platform rather than a land registry, which is the only way a property register is being built in this base.

summary: A [National Payments Systems Vision and Strategy 2026-2030](2026-04-16-rbm-national-payments-strategy-2026-2030-itweb) was launched in April 2026, above a [national switch](2026-04-16-rbm-national-payments-strategy-2026-2030-itweb) operating since 2015.
developments:
The strategy prioritises infrastructure expansion and affordability for low-income users, cybersecurity and resilience to power and connectivity failure, regulatory modernisation, financial technology innovation and regional integration, with the deputy governor acknowledging persistent rural gaps; no targets, budget or milestone dates are stated and the document itself is not held ([strategy](2026-04-16-rbm-national-payments-strategy-2026-2030-itweb)).

The switch has linked banks, mobile money platforms and cash machines since 2015, with an instant bank transfer service live on it from June 2025, real-time to any Malawian bank up to MWK 500m by short code ([transfer](2025-06-17-paychangu-centenary-instant-bank-transfer-malswitch-malawi24), [infrastructure](2026-04-24-paychangu-unified-payment-infrastructure-wearetech)).

progress: Mixed, mobile money value up 94 per cent in a year while the cost of replacing worn banknotes rose 38 per cent
summary: Mobile money reached [MWK 37.9tn in 2025, up 94 per cent](2026-03-30-mobile-money-k38tn-2025-nps-report-times), while [banknote replacement is expected to cost MWK 69.8bn in 2026](2026-07-25-malawi-cash-reliance-banknote-costs-digital-payment-uptake).
developments:
Value ran at MWK 19.5tn on 1.8bn transactions in 2024 ([2024](2025-04-16 Mobile money deals hit K19.5tn in 2024)) and MWK 37.9tn on 2.4bn transactions in 2025, with subscriptions at 19.9m of which 44.8 per cent were active in a thirty-day window; airtime was 42 per cent of transactions, cash-in and cash-out 33.1 per cent and merchant payments 7.7 per cent ([2025](2026-03-30-mobile-money-k38tn-2025-nps-report-times)). The central bank cautions that the subscription figure counts registered wallets.

Replacing worn banknotes cost MWK 50.6bn in 2025 and is expected to cost MWK 69.8bn in 2026, about 38 per cent higher ([banknotes](2026-07-25-malawi-cash-reliance-banknote-costs-digital-payment-uptake)); an economists' association president named government levies on digital money transfers as a reason cash use persists ([banknotes](2026-07-25-malawi-cash-reliance-banknote-costs-digital-payment-uptake)).

summary: Mobile money was [integrated into the agricultural marketing corporation](2026-06-24-airtel-money-admarc-farmer-payments-itweb) so farmers are paid into wallets, and [card e-commerce acceptance](2026-08-19-standard-bank-expands-unionpay-acceptance) opened to merchants.
developments:
The integration lets farmers be paid directly into mobile wallets and customers pay electronically for commodities across the corporation's national market and depot network; no volume, value or farmer count is held ([integration](2026-06-24-airtel-money-admarc-farmer-payments-itweb)).

Online acceptance of an international card scheme opened to participating merchants in August 2026, settling in local currency, dollars or both, as part of an extension to nine African markets; no Malawi-specific merchant count is given ([acceptance](2026-08-19-standard-bank-expands-unionpay-acceptance), [extension](2026-08-19-tan-unionpay-standard-bank-nine-african-markets)).

summary: A [regional retail payments corridor with Zambia](2025-10-13 Comesa payment system connects Malawi, Zambia) is the first interoperable cross-border system in local currencies, with a scheme rulebook published in August 2026.
developments:
The corridor links the two countries in local currencies without foreign exchange, supervised by both central banks, with three Malawian early adopters ([corridor](2025-10-13 Comesa payment system connects Malawi, Zambia)).

The clearing house published the scheme rulebook setting operational and governance rules for instant low-cost cross-border retail payments, alongside a gender audit and strategy to 2030 drawing on research along the corridor ([rulebook](2026-08-10-comesa-clearing-house-drpp-scheme-rulebook-gender-strategy)). No volume or value figure for the corridor is held.

summary: A [National e-Payment Gateway](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times) is designed as the single entry point for all government collections, under a [fiscal governance programme](2024-04-26 Malawi Fiscal Governance Program-for-Results - PAD (World Bank)) of about US$80m.
developments:
The gateway was described as a 2025 breakthrough despite integration hurdles, supported by a financial inclusion project and a development bank; no live date, transaction figure or agency coverage is stated, and one dated account is all the base holds ([gateway](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)).

A fiscal governance programme of SDR 60.3m, about US$80m equivalent at appraisal, supports revenue mobilisation, budget execution and procurement modernisation including e-procurement digitalisation ([programme](2024-04-26 Malawi Fiscal Governance Program-for-Results - PAD (World Bank))); the base carries no implementation, disbursement or results reporting after the appraisal document ([programme](2024-04-26 Malawi Fiscal Governance Program-for-Results - PAD (World Bank))).

progress: Mixed, a tariff-notice breach enforced with customer compensation while an interoperability order's compliance year passed with nothing on file
summary: The regulator [found both operators in breach of the tariff-notice requirement](2026-07-17-macra-airtel-malawi-tnm-tariff-compensation) and ordered customer compensation, while a [mobile-money interoperability order](2025-07-16-cftc-tnm-mpamba-eticketing-interoperability-malawi24) expired unreported.
developments:
Both mobile operators were found in breach in respect of a notice window in mid-2026 and agreed to credit affected customers with bundles equal to the price difference by 31 July with evidence of compliance, alongside strengthened internal procedures; the approved price increase itself stands, so what was enforced is notice and not price ([order](2026-07-17-macra-airtel-malawi-tnm-tariff-compensation), [compliance](2026-07-17-malawi-macra-telecom-tariff-compliance), [refund](2026-07-21-airtel-tnm-ordered-refund-malawi-customers)). The base holds no confirmation that compensation was completed.

A competition order of July 2025 required a mobile-money operator to open its exclusive football ticketing platform to other providers within a year, with concurrent physical ticketing for six months and progress reports every ninety days; the compliance year expired around July 2026 and nothing held records opening, a progress report or an enforcement step ([interoperability](2025-07-16-cftc-tnm-mpamba-eticketing-interoperability-malawi24)).

summary: The [Electronic Invoicing System](2026-01-21-mra-public-notice-transition-efds-to-eis) reached full enforcement in May 2026, with [8,552 taxpayers registered](2026-07-20-malawi24-mra-electronic-invoicing-system-momentum) and [collections above US$28m in a month](2026-06-03 Malawi reaps digital tax gains).
developments:
The system was established under the amended value added tax statute, with migration off older fiscal devices required from August 2025, regulations published in January 2026, the transition period ending that month and full enforcement with penalties from 1 May 2026 after the authority rescheduled ([transition](2026-01-21-mra-public-notice-transition-efds-to-eis), [clarification](2026-02-11-malawi24-mra-clarifies-eis-rental-income-tax)).

About 7,500 of roughly 9,000 registered operators had migrated by June 2026, rising to 8,552 registered by July ([registered](2026-06-03 Malawi reaps digital tax gains), [momentum](2026-07-20-malawi24-mra-electronic-invoicing-system-momentum)).

Collections through it run at over US$1.2m a day, with May 2026 above US$28m ([revenue](2026-06-03 Malawi reaps digital tax gains)); the authority collects in kwacha and the publisher gives only a dollar rendering with no rate or conversion date ([revenue](2026-06-03 Malawi reaps digital tax gains)).

summary: The [health management information system](2025-10-21 Utilisation of data and factors affecting the performance of the Health Management Information System (HMIS). The case of six Synods of Livingstonia health facilities in Malawi) is in operation but weakly used, on fieldwork across six faith-based facilities in three districts.
developments:
Seventy per cent of facility respondents used the system's data against 33.3 per cent of district respondents, 31.4 per cent of facility staff had had no data-handling training in twenty-four months, supervisory visits reached under half of facilities, and there were no standard operating procedures for data management ([study](2025-10-21 Utilisation of data and factors affecting the performance of the Health Management Information System (HMIS). The case of six Synods of Livingstonia health facilities in Malawi)).

The sample is six faith-based facilities in three districts rather than national, and nothing later is held, so the position is carried forward rather than re-established.

summary: A [Crime Management System](2026-07-29-undp-malawi-police-crime-management-system) covering the case cycle from report to final disposal is in pilot, with officers trained as early adopters.
developments:
A three-day technical training opened in Lilongwe in July 2026 ahead of a nationwide rollout ([training](2026-07-29-undp-malawi-police-crime-management-system)).

No procurement value, named supplier or rollout date is published, and nothing is stated on how case-file personal data is handled under the data protection statute. It is framed by the implementing partner through its governance portfolio rather than by the police.

summary: A [customs data exchange arrangement with South Africa](2026-08-12-malawi-south-africa-customs-data-exchange-arrangement) was signed for real-time exchange, above a [national single window](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times) launched in 2025.
developments:
The arrangement establishes a secure electronic platform for real-time customs data exchange aligned to an international data model, with both authorities agreeing to fast-track implementation; no go-live date, purpose-limitation, retention or reciprocity terms are published, and the counterpart authority notified the updated arrangement and published a draft rule amendment in August 2026 ([arrangement](2026-08-12-malawi-south-africa-customs-data-exchange-arrangement), [sharing](2026-08-05-malawi-sa-digital-customs-data-sharing), [exchange](2026-08-05-malawi-south-africa-customs-data-exchange)).

The counterpart supplied about 18 per cent of the country's imports, US$3bn in 2025/26, which is what makes the exchange material ([window](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)). A national single window integrating trade-related agencies launched in May 2025 and no later position is held ([window](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)).

progress: Mixed, e-procurement made mandatory nationwide while passport applicants who filed a year earlier are overtaken by same-day issuances
summary: [E-procurement became mandatory](2026-04-01-ppda-mandatory-e-procurement-maneps-malawi24) for all public entities in April 2026, while the [passport system](2026-07-21-malawi24-mangochi-passport-printing-resumes) carries an unresolved backlog and [queue transparency](2026-07-21-malawi24-mp-demands-passport-queue-reform) is only accepted in principle.
developments:
The electronic procurement system built under the foundations project became mandatory nationwide from 1 April 2026 under a March directive covering all public entities, with remote submission and registration; no post-mandate uptake figure, tender count or exception list is held ([mandate](2026-04-01-ppda-mandatory-e-procurement-maneps-malawi24), [initiative](2024-01-01 The National Digitalization Initiative Transforming Public Procurement in Malawi)).

A US$29.9m passport contract awarded in January 2025 had a troubled transition and a backlog of over 100,000 applications ([contract](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)); printing resumed at Mangochi in July 2026, and a member told the House that applicants who filed nine months to a year earlier are being overtaken by same-day issuances ([printing](2026-07-21-malawi24-mangochi-passport-printing-resumes), [queue](2026-07-21-malawi24-mp-demands-passport-queue-reform)).

A sequence number at application, message notification and an online portal were accepted in principle and deferred until the passport system stabilises ([transparency](2026-07-21-malawi24-mp-demands-passport-queue-reform)), and an electronic auctions platform is being scoped to replace paper government auctions ([auctions](2026-08-19-malawi-digitises-public-auction-platform)).

summary: The [first local-authority ICT policy and standards](2026-05-20-local-authorities-ict-policy-dowa-malawi24) were validated in May 2026, and a [successor governance project](2026-07-30-malawi-ida-130m-grants-gesd2-thrive-parliament-approval) covers 32 councils to 2031.
developments:
Councils had operated with no framework beyond the national digitalisation policy, a 2022 situational analysis having found weak ICT support, absent council projects and ICT excluded from procurement; the first dedicated local-authority policy plus standards were validated in May 2026 with councils being sensitised, and no adoption date is held ([policy](2026-05-20-local-authorities-ict-policy-dowa-malawi24)).

The successor project is an SDR 58.2m grant, about US$80m equivalent, ratified in July 2026 and closing in 2031, covering 32 councils with four entering for the first time, of which a US$12.8m subcomponent funds business-process re-engineering, software and hardware assessments and a performance dashboard ([project](2026-07-30-malawi-ida-130m-grants-gesd2-thrive-parliament-approval), [appraisal](2026-03-31-worldbank-malawi-gesd2-pad-p508024)).

Its predecessor closed in June 2026 with its grant mechanism continuing ([predecessor](2026-07-30-malawi-ida-130m-grants-gesd2-thrive-parliament-approval)), so process re-engineering is funded ahead of equipment purchase.

progress: Mixed, a real-time constituency fund dashboard launched while clean council audit opinions fell from 22 to 18
summary: A [real-time dashboard](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight) tracks more than 2,000 constituency projects, [27 of 28 councils qualified for performance grants](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight), and [clean audit opinions fell to 18](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight).
developments:
The dashboard was launched in July 2026 carrying project progress, budgets and locations for more than 2,000 development projects, with citizens asked to raise concerns through channels on it and named ministers given real-time access ([launch](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight)); the launching minister stated its currency depends on councils uploading information manually, and no platform address is established in anything held, so none of it can be inspected ([launch](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight), [dashboard](2026-08-01-phiri-unveils-game-changing-cdf-dashboard-to-fast-track-development-end-delays), [parliament](2026-08-03-chipungu-roars-in-malawi-parliament-cdf-dashboard-will-expose-every-dodgy-project), [channels](2026-08-04-govt-urges-communities-to-use-new-cdf-dashboard-to-report-project-concerns)).

Twenty-seven of twenty-eight district councils qualified for performance-based grants on the 2025/26 assessment ([assessment](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight), [indicator](2026-03-31-worldbank-malawi-gesd2-pad-p508024)), while councils receiving clean audit opinions fell from 22 in 2023/24 to 18 in 2024/25 with one adverse opinion ([audits](2026-07-31-malawi-real-time-cdf-dashboard-council-oversight)).

A second-city council has partnered a bank to digitise revenue and tax collection, with no go-live date or collection figure held ([revenue](2026-03-06 Malawi's second city digitises tax collection)).

progress: Mixed, a corporate programme connecting 36 schools against 85 per cent of the country's 9,000 schools with limited or no internet
summary: [85 per cent of 9,000 schools have limited or no internet](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24) and about 900 have none, while a [corporate programme has connected 36](2026-07-15-airtel-malawi-schools).
developments:
Lack of electricity and of digital devices are named as the main barriers; a development bank is separately supporting connection of over 200 schools and the acceleration project targets 2,000 ([analysis](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24), [targets](2025-06-24 Malawi boosts digital economy with connectivity, plans 2M digital ID enrollments)).

The corporate programme has connected 36 schools with a further nine scheduled in 2026, equipped laboratories with televisions and tablets, zero-rated twelve local learning sites and states more than 32,000 learners and over 900 teachers benefiting ([programme](2026-07-15-airtel-malawi-schools)); all figures are the company's own ([programme](2026-07-15-airtel-malawi-schools)).

summary: A university [commissioned an artificial-intelligence fertigation system](2026-07-17-malawi-must-ai-fertigation) automating irrigation and fertiliser application from real-time crop data.
developments:
The system was commissioned in July 2026 at the university's Thyolo campus with an assisted smart tree nursery, under a continental agricultural-universities programme ([facility](2026-07-17-malawi-must-ai-fertigation)).

It is a single university facility rather than a national system, and no cost or funding source is stated. It is the only working sectoral use of the technology in the base for the country.

summary: The defence force [intends to adopt artificial intelligence in military operations and to learn it from the Chinese army](2026-07-24-times-mw-mdf-ai-warfare-china), with no doctrine, oversight body or civilian-control provision on file.
developments:
The intention was stated by the defence minister at an anniversary event in Lilongwe, in a relationship stated to extend past exchanges into specialised training, equipment supply and institutional development, with further equipment, capacity building and command-level training under discussion ([intention](2026-07-24-times-mw-mdf-ai-warfare-china)).

No Malawian doctrine, oversight body, budget line or civilian-control provision for military artificial intelligence is on file, and the draft national strategy as reported does not cover it. That gap is the finding.

summary: A [low-resource language data trust](2026-06-24-chichewa-ai-language-data-trust-techafricanews) is assembling licensed Chichewa content as artificial-intelligence training data, with no dataset or licence terms published.
developments:
The initiative was launched at a national workshop in Lilongwe in June 2026, supported by a development bank and a foundation, and is developing core frameworks alongside the content ([trust](2026-06-24-chichewa-ai-language-data-trust-techafricanews)).

No dataset, licence terms, governance structure or release is published. A data trust holding licensed language content raises rights and consent questions the announcement does not address.

progress: Stalled, two licensed entrants have never launched and a third has never mattered, with a new licensing round only announced
summary: [Additional operator licences are under consideration](2026-07-18-namalomba-parliament-new-operators-nyasatimes), while [one licensee](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition) missed a 2023 launch target and [another licensed in 2022](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition) has announced no date.
developments:
The minister told Parliament that the President had authorised the ministry to identify an investor able to build a network without delay, conceding that foreign-exchange shortages constrain incumbents' equipment imports and that earlier licensees who took spectrum without launching had licences revoked, ending in litigation; no bid timetable, licence terms or spectrum allocation is stated ([round](2026-07-18-namalomba-parliament-new-operators-nyasatimes), [competition](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition), [pressure](2026-07-24-malawi24-mp-pushes-third-telecom-player)).

One licensee targeted a late-2023 commercial launch, was delayed by macroeconomic conditions and has announced no new date ([first](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition)); another licensed in 2022 has announced no launch date either ([second](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition)).

A third operator licensed in 2007 holds a small share available mainly in major cities and has not significantly challenged the duopoly ([third](2026-07-20-malawi-seeks-new-telecom-competition)).

summary: [ICT services exports rose from about US$70m in 2020 to US$154m in 2023](2026-06-06-ict-services-exports-k270bn-ictam-expo-malawi24) on an industry account, and a [payment aggregator](2026-04-24-paychangu-unified-payment-infrastructure-wearetech) connects mobile money, cards and bank transfers through one integration.
developments:
The export series was cited by a private-sector managing director as evidence that the sector already earns foreign currency; the underlying figures are dollars, undated as to conversion, and are an industry speaker's rather than an official statistic ([exports](2026-06-06-ict-services-exports-k270bn-ictam-expo-malawi24)).

The aggregator was founded in 2021 and offers small-business tools including interfaces, plugins, payment links, invoicing and analytics; the profile is company-reported throughout and carries no dated event, transaction volume or revenue figure ([aggregator](2026-04-24-paychangu-unified-payment-infrastructure-wearetech), [transfers](2025-06-17-paychangu-centenary-instant-bank-transfer-malswitch-malawi24)).

summary: An operator [announced artificial-intelligence laboratories and innovation hubs](2025-11-10-tnm-30-years-ai-labs-times) for 2026 with nothing opened, and a [university innovation lab](2019-01-01-undp-mwi-mubas-lab-2019-mubas-innovation-lab-malawi-university-of) grant reaches its scheduled end this year.
developments:
The laboratories were announced at the operator's thirtieth-anniversary event for establishment in 2026, to let Malawians build artificial-intelligence-driven services; no site, budget, partner or opening date is stated and nothing on record shows one has opened ([laboratories](2025-11-10-tnm-30-years-ai-labs-times)).

A grant of US$1,880,499 committed in 2019 equips a university innovation hub for ideation, prototyping, mentorship and incubation, with a scheduled end year of 2026 and no closure or extension on file ([hub](2019-01-01-undp-mwi-mubas-lab-2019-mubas-innovation-lab-malawi-university-of)); the total budget is stated as US$3.19m against that commitment ([hub](2019-01-01-undp-mwi-mubas-lab-2019-mubas-innovation-lab-malawi-university-of)).

summary: [Over 19,000 young people](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities), 10,000 of them female, were trained through ten technology hubs to 2024, and a [second entrepreneurs lab](2026-08-17-giz-malawi-ai-digital-skills-mzuzu) ran in Mzuzu in 2026.
developments:
The training figure is cumulative over 2017 to 2024 rather than an annual rate, and no successor training count is published; the acceleration project's own training indicators are not reported in this base ([training](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities)).

A second edition of an artificial-intelligence and digital solutions lab trained 24 entrepreneurs from four northern districts in tools for marketing, customer engagement and financial management, under German and European programmes; no cohort total across editions, curriculum, certification or follow-up measure is stated ([lab](2026-08-17-giz-malawi-ai-digital-skills-mzuzu), [initiative](2026-08-17-german-eu-initiative-boosts-malawian-ai)).

summary: A corporate fund [awarded its first 25 undergraduate places](2026-08-18-airtel-malawi-tech-scholarships) at the science and technology university, covering tuition, stipend, accommodation, data and a connectivity device.
developments:
The first beneficiaries were named in August 2026, seven months after launch, drawn from seventeen districts and taking eight programmes including computer systems, cyber security, sustainable energy engineering and metallurgy ([award](2026-08-18-airtel-malawi-tech-scholarships), [launch](2026-01-07-airtel-nzeru-fund-stem-scholarships-malawi24)).

One cohort of 25 is now filled and no continuation commitment beyond it is stated; the announced degree list at award is wider than the computing fields the launch named.

summary: An [e-learning programme](2019-01-01-kfw-mwi-001-unlocking-talent-e-learning-fur-primarbildung-unlocking) for tablet-based learning centres in primary schools and teacher training colleges closed at the end of 2024 with no successor.
developments:
A grant of EUR 12,996,804 committed in 2019 was almost fully disbursed at US$14,522,971 of US$14,549,922, and the programme closed at the end of 2024 ([programme](2019-01-01-kfw-mwi-001-unlocking-talent-e-learning-fur-primarbildung-unlocking)).

The plan was 178 primary-school learning centres and eight mobile centres, and no delivery figure is held. No successor programme, evaluation or continuation is on file, so the country's largest school digital-learning investment ended without a published result.

progress: Mixed, a universal service fund evaluating device subsidies while its own resourcing is stated as insufficient
summary: The [Universal Service Fund](2026-08-21-malawi-targets-smartphone-tax-relief) is funded from the regulator's budget and stated to be insufficient, while [85 per cent of schools have limited or no internet](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24).
developments:
The fund runs a school connectivity project providing computer equipment and secondary-school skills work is stated to draw on it, but the Director General stated existing funding levels remain insufficient for the country's connectivity needs, and no income, balance or disbursement figure is held for any year ([fund](2026-03-26-dmap-90-telecom-towers-rural-connectivity-techafricanews), [skills](2026-07-10-macra-undp-ai-digital-id-collaboration-itweb)). The regulator said in August 2026 it is evaluating fund mechanisms to subsidise consumer devices and fund digital-literacy work, including a proposed one-tablet-one-student programme ([subsidies](2026-08-21-malawi-targets-smartphone-tax-relief)).

Eighty-five per cent of the country's 9,000 schools have limited or no internet access and about 900 have none, with lack of electricity and devices the main barriers ([schools](2026-04-17-school-connectivity-unicef-giga-report-malawi24), [support](2025-06-23 Digitalizing Malawi to improve access to education, public services, and income opportunities)).

summary: A [fourth national ICT survey](2026-08-14-malawi-national-ict-survey-nso-macra) is in the field across all districts covering 12,000 households, with its field-staff recruitment publicly questioned.
developments:
The survey covers mobile and computer ownership, internet access, digital financial services, e-commerce and cybersecurity awareness, including the refugee camp at Dzaleka, run by the statistical office with the communications regulator to inform national planning; no publication date for the results is stated ([survey](2026-08-14-malawi-national-ict-survey-nso-macra)).

Field-supervisor and enumerator recruitment drew public questions when training opened in August 2026; the base holds the complaint and no response to it, and a survey whose fieldwork staffing is contested is one whose results will be read against that ([recruitment](2026-08-19-malawi24-nso-macra-ict-survey-jobs)).

summary: The [National Payments System Report series](2026-03-30-mobile-money-k38tn-2025-nps-report-times) continues quarterly and annually, and a [public sector reforms information system](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times) tracks agencies against reform targets.
developments:
The payments series is in publication with the 2024 annual report reported in April 2025 ([2024](2025-04-16 Mobile money deals hit K19.5tn in 2024)), a quarterly report in November 2025 ([quarterly](2025-11-18 Malawi Hits 20 Million Mobile Money Subscribers Amid Rising Digital Payments)) and the 2025 annual report in March 2026 ([2025](2026-03-30-mobile-money-k38tn-2025-nps-report-times)); the base holds the reports only through press accounts ([growth](2025-01-22 National payment system registers growth in 2024 Quarter 3)).

A reforms information system launched in December 2025 as a dedicated platform tracking how agencies perform against reform targets, with no user, coverage or output figure held ([reforms](2026-01-13-ict-sector-2025-implementation-woes-times)).

Against those, the copyright levy is distributed entirely on records submitted by licensed disc-burning centres rather than on digital consumption, and tax reconciliation against a rights holder's taxpayer number is not automatic ([levy](2026-08-04-malawi24-cosoma-cd-burning-data-royalty-payouts)).

summary: The electoral commission [refused an observer coalition analysable electronic copies of the voter roll](2025-06-08 MEC Rejects Observer Coalition's Electronic Voter Register Access Request), and the same position stands after the elections.
developments:
The commission held that the elections statute limits inspection to verification of entries at registration centres and regional offices; the request explicitly excluded biometric data, and the commission published the correspondence itself ([refusal](2025-06-08 MEC Rejects Observer Coalition's Electronic Voter Register Access Request)).

Nothing held records a later request, appeal or change of practice, including after the September 2025 elections. It is the base's only recorded test of machine-readable access to a government dataset in the country.

progress: Mixed, concessional fibre lending and a defence artificial-intelligence relationship against a rejected surveillance package
summary: Two [concessional loans](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-693-million) financed the fibre backbone, the [defence force intends to learn military artificial intelligence](2026-07-24-times-mw-mdf-ai-warfare-china) from China, and the country [rejected a safe-city surveillance package](2023-09-27-ids-mapping-supply-surveillance-technologies-africa-1bn).
developments:
The backbone's second phase was financed at CNY 693,000,000 over twenty years, on-lent to the electricity utility with first repayment falling due in March 2027 ([loan](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-693-million), [first phase](2016-01-01-eximbank-cn-mwi-001-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-1554-million)).

The defence relationship is stated to extend past exchanges into specialised training, equipment supply and institutional development, with command-level training under discussion ([defence](2026-07-24-times-mw-mdf-ai-warfare-china)).

Malawi is the only one of five countries studied to have rejected the safe-city surveillance package offered by Chinese companies, and the base holds no account of who rejected it, when, or on what grounds ([rejection](2023-09-27-ids-mapping-supply-surveillance-technologies-africa-1bn)).
